newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares ease, unsettled by EMU talk.
newsitem.headline: German shares ease, unsettled by EMU talk.

text.p: German shares took on an easier trend on Monday as dealers said speculation about the start of Europe's monetary union added a degree of confusion to a market that already appeared keen to take a breather.
The softer dollar and German debt market were also seen facilitating the downward move but no fundamental weakness or significant correction was thought imminently likely.
"Markets around Europe are a bit drifty but we don't see any real selling (in the German market)," one trader said.
The IBIS-DAX index traded 48.10 points lower at 3,356.19 on what were described as thin volumes.

Speculation had been fuelled about a possible delay to the launch of EMU by an article in the Bild newspaper quoting German finance minister Theo Waigel as saying that adherence to the EMU criteria was more important than to the timetable.
Despite a raft of assurances emerging from a meeting of EU finance ministers in Brussels, dealers said that was enough to keep some investors on the sidelines for the time being.
German M3 money supply data and the latest Ifo business climate survey, both due later this week, were seen as possible buying catalysts indirectly through the bond market.

Further uncertainty was evident ahead of the expiry of the key March DAX future later this week, an event which often creates a degree of turbulence in the main cash market. descent in afternoon IBIS trade, falling 3.65 marks or 3.85 percent to 91.20 after publishing 1996 earnings that disappointed some analysts earlier on.
Cosmetics and medication maker Beiersdorf slumped five marks to 90, albeit among slim volumes, after its Tesa adhesives tape unit said a 1997 fall in turnover was possible.
